title: Upcoming event
description: One event, as published in a per-source feed or a combined one. The shape is identical in both: sources is always an array, so a consumer parses them the same way.

id.description: "{source}:{guid}". THE identifier, unique within every feed and every combined feed. Source-scoped because ps_events UIDs are per-site sequences, not a global namespace: ps_events:4056:delta:0 is ai's "ORFE Colloquium" and materials' "Materials Institute Symposium", two unrelated events.

guid.description: The upstream UID, verbatim. Source-scoped and NOT unique across feeds -- that is what makes consumer-side de-duplication possible at all. Published because it is what the campus ingest keys on.

sources.description: Every registered source whose feed carried this exact event. Length 1 in a per-source feed; longer in a combined feed means two or more units published an identical listing and this record represents both. Never a scalar, in any output.

platform.description: Checked against the feed's PRODID rather than assumed: kellercenter serves a Drupal iCal feed from a URL that looks like every Site Builder one.

startsAt.description: The absolute instant, canonical UTC. Compared as a string throughout -- for ordering, for de-duplication, and for byte-stable output -- so the form has to be canonical or string comparison stops meaning instant comparison.

startTime.description: Local wall clock, no offset. The predecessor's published shape, retained because the campus ingest parses it. Never compare this across sources.

title.description: Never empty. When the feed carries none -- ORFE's SUMMARY is the speaker, and quantum posts 14 of 18 titles as TBD -- one is synthesized, and titleSource and titleIsPlaceholder say so.

speakers.description: Every speaker. An event can have several: bioengineering's Rising Stars symposium lists four.

speaker.description: Derived from speakers, for the existing campus ingest. One speaker renders "Name, Affiliation"; several join with "; " -- not a comma, which already separates a name from its affiliation.

affiliation.description: Derived: the affiliation when one applies to the whole event, empty when the speakers disagree. Picking the first would attribute one person's institution to the panel.

series.description: The feed's CATEGORIES joined with a bare comma, in feed order. Downstream code splits on that comma.

tags.description: Canonical tags -- what combined-feed predicates match on. Only ever canonical: a final public oral examination reaches these feeds under four spellings, and "exclude FPOs" is meaningless without one name for it.

rawCategories.description: Categories exactly as the feed spelled them.

unmappedTags.description: Categories no canonical tag recognised. Published rather than only counted, so a department inventing a series is visible to a consumer as well as to a maintainer.

name.description: The venue. An unsplittable value belongs here whole rather than guessed apart.

id.description: Reserved for a canonical venue id; normally empty.

detail.description: The room, when one could be identified without guessing.

summaryRaw.description: The untouched SUMMARY, so a mapping decision can be re-examined from published output alone.

mappingRules.description: The rule that mapped this event, as "{source}:{rule}". A reordering that reclassifies events still produces valid output, so the recorded rule is what makes it visible.

summaryRest.description: Text a rule parked rather than guessing which field it belonged to.

titleSource.description: Where the title came from. ics and enriched mean a department wrote it; every fallback means this pipeline synthesized it.

titleIsPlaceholder.description: True when the title was synthesized. A consumer must always be able to tell; the predecessor publishes a literal "TBD" with neither this nor titleSource set.
